title: Module B — LLM Evidence & Confidence Layer
description: Output of the Gemini evidence module. One document per repository. Produces a repo summary and, per skill, a natural-language justification plus the Evidence Score itself. Change of plan (see shared/README.md): Gemini now assigns confidence directly, so REPOSITORY_SKILL.confidence is written straight from this document — there is no separate deterministic evidence-scoring step, and this module no longer depends on Module A's raw features to compute a score (README_text may still be used as prompt context, but is not required input).

prompt_version.description: Bump when the scoring prompt changes. This is now the only 'formula version' in the system — there is no separate scoring-formula version, since the model assigns confidence directly.

repo_summary.description: One-paragraph description of what the repository does. Written once at ingestion, reused for every JD.

skills.description: Skills the model found evidence for, each with the Evidence Score assigned directly. A row here is written straight to REPOSITORY_SKILL — no downstream re-scoring.

skill_id.description: Resolved against the SKILL vocabulary when the label matches a canonical skill; null when the model proposed a skill outside the vocabulary.

confidence.description: Evidence Score for this repository-skill pair, assigned directly by the model — not computed by a downstream formula. Written straight to REPOSITORY_SKILL.confidence. Means 'the model found strong evidence', not 'probability the candidate knows the skill'.

nl_evidence.description: How the skill shows up in this repo, in one sentence, and the basis for the confidence value above. Goes into SKILL_EVIDENCE.evidence and later into ai_summarize.

semantic_similarity.description: Optional supporting signal: cosine similarity between the canonical skill description embedding and the repo content embedding. No longer feeds a scoring formula — kept for inspection only.

referenced_files.description: Files the model cited when writing nl_evidence, so the confidence value can be checked.
